title: Planning Commission And National Development Council NDC History
definition: The Planning Commission was a non-constitutional, extra-constitutional, and non-statutory body established in March 1950 by an executive resolution of the Government of India to formulate India's Five-Year Plans, while the National Development Council (NDC), established in August 1952, served as the apex body for policy decision-making and deliberations on development in India, securing cooperation of states in execution of plans.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for General Studies Paper III (Indian Economy, Planning, Mobilization of Resources, Inclusive Growth) and General Studies Paper II (Federal Polity, Centre-State Relations, Inter-State Council vs NDC). Tested extensively in Prelims regarding statutory status, composition, and historical evolution leading up to NITI Aayog.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Planning Commission And National Development Council NDC History.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and federal dynamics between Centre and States.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Basic federal structure of Indian polity
